title: Tenant KEK proxy for regional residency, retention tagging, and attestation simulator
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers need a way to: 1) use tenant-managed keys (BYOK/KEK) scoped to geographic residency, 2) have retention-aware encryption metadata attached to objects so retention and deletion workflows can be validated by legal/compliance, and 3) produce attestation artifacts that simulate live key operations for audit pipelines without touching production KMS/HSM keys. Goals: build a KEK-proxy service that mediates tenant KEK usage across regions, stamps retention/residency metadata into encryption envelopes, and offers an "attestation simulator" mode to generate deterministic, replayable audit artifacts for compliance testing and automated evidence exports. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, and an initial integration with the evidence-export pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: KEK-proxy accepts BYOK connections and routes key wrap/unwrap requests to the correct regional KMS/HSM endpoint based on tenant residency policy
Encryption envelopes include a signed retention/residency tag (region, policy-id, retention-expiry) that the runtime and evidence-export pipeline can read
Attestation simulator mode can generate a time-sequenced stream of signing/unwrap events and audit records that match production schema without using production keys

Integration test showing a tenant in EU region with a 365-day retention policy: object gets wrapped with correct metadata, simulator produces the expected attestation bundle, and export pipeline ingests the bundle into the compliance datastore
Performance regression: added latency from runtime -> KEK-proxy -> KMS must be < 12ms P50 for wrap operations under normal load; document fallback behavior when latency SLOs are breached
Automated evidence export (S3/secure-store) created by CI job using simulator mode and validated by compliance checklist
tasks: Design API for KEK-proxy (wrap/unwrap/status) and metadata schema for retention/residency tags
Prototype KEK-proxy with pluggable KMS adapters (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK, Azure, and HSM proxy)
Implement attestation simulator that emits signed audit records with deterministic IDs and timestamps
Add retention/residency stamping into server-side envelope creation codepath
End-to-end tests: integrate simulator with evidence-exporter and validate ingest schema
Load test KEK-proxy and measure added latency and error modes
Security review and threat model update for proxy and simulator modes
Documentation: Confluence design doc, runbook for on-call, and sample compliance export job
comments: 2025-11-12 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after compliance workshop; initial scope agreed with PM and Legal. Targeting a prototype-first approach to avoid blocking Dedicated customers.

2025-11-13 - Daniel Kim: Spike started to validate KMS adapter interfaces; AWS KMS and a mock HSM adapter are functional. Noted that HSM proxy introduces additional latency that needs accounting in rollout policies.

2025-11-15 - Miguel Ortega (Security): Suggested simulator output must be cryptographically separated from production keys and include verifiable chain-of-custody metadata. Requested embedding a simulator certificate that is rotated independently.
2025-11-18 - PM (Sofie Müller): Reviewed acceptance criteria; added requirement for CI-generated attestation bundles for quarterly audits. Asked for example Confluence export template.

2025-11-19 - Daniel Kim: Implemented retention tag schema v0.1 and pushed design doc to Confluence (link below). Began basic integration test with evidence-exporter; CI job failing due to missing ingest schema mapping. Creating ENG-28192 to fix mapper.

2025-11-20 - Aisha Patel: Security review kick-off scheduled. Noted dependency on ENG-17205 for key residency policy service; raised a concern about corner-case where multi-region keys will require double-wrap semantics. Follow-up spike planned.
notes: This approach intentionally separates simulator artifacts from production audit trails so compliance can rehearse audits without exposing customer KMS material. Long-term: consider merging simulator into the evidence-export microservice or exposing a replayable fixture format for external auditors.
open_questions: Should simulator mode be accessible to customers in Dedicated/private deployments or restricted to Redwood-managed compliance tenants?
What key proofing/verification do auditors need in simulator mode to accept synthetic bundles?
Do we need an operator-controlled toggle to inject simulated failures (unwrap errors, HSM timeouts) for resilience testing?
